statement: The receipt reconstructs the failure record from surviving evidence. It does not claim to have been emitted by the failed execution.
why_reconstruction_was_necessary: Specification section 25 requires a failure receipt with fourteen named fields. PERSIST.write_failure_receipt and T1DevelopmentRun.failure_receipt were both implemented, but no caller invoked either and t1_canonical_driver.execute contained no exception handler, so the exception propagated to the interpreter and the specification's mandated artifact was never written. The gap was closed for future runs by PR #49.

why_unrecoverable_in_place: Specification section 17 requires the held-out state trace AND evaluation evidence to be persisted once. Only the trace was persisted, by widening it into the stage-23 OOF store; the per-fold confusion counts, episode evidence and onset latencies lived in run.held_out_traces and were destroyed with the process. Fixed for future runs by PR #50.

reconstruction.not_reconstructed_reason: These were never persisted and cannot be derived from the label-free artifacts that survive. Recovering them is the whole purpose of the authorized measurement continuation, and inventing them here would be fabricating evidence.

known_stale_in_the_consumed_attempt.T1_RUN_STATUS.json: reads status STARTED with updated_at equal to the claim timestamp, and label_blind_input_opened / held_out_labels_opened_for_folds / oof_evidence_promoted all false. Every one of those was false at 19:47:24 and none was true at 19:57:57. It is left exactly as the run wrote it: a failed attempt is not rewritten to look clean.
